Baanah the son of Hushai, was one of Solomon's twelve regional administrators, having jurisdiction over Asher and Aloth (1 Kings 4:16).
Baaraedit

Baara (בָּעֲרָא "in a hurry") was one of the three wives of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, according to 1 Chronicles 8:8.

Baaseiahedit

Baaseiah (Hebrew:באשעיה Meaning: the Lord is bold) was a Gershonite Levite as the son of Michael and the father of Malkijah according 1 Chronicles 6:25. He was also an ancestor of Asaph the seer or poet.

Bakbakkaredit

Bakbakkar (בַּקְבַּקַּר "searcher"),[147] according to the Hebrew Bible, was a Levite dwelling in the villages of the Netophathites, and later carried captive into Babylon. (1 Chronicles 9:15) He is also one of the descendants of Asaph.

Bakbukedit

Bakbuk (meaning: "bottle" perhaps onomatopoetic), was the ancestor of the children of Bakbuk who were among the Nethinim and returned from Babylon (Ezra 2:51; Nehemiah 7:53).

Bakbukiahedit

Bakbukiah (בַּקְבֻּקְיָה) was the name of 2 biblical figures.

A Levite who dwelt in Jerusalem who returned from captivity (Nehemiah 11:17); perhaps the same in Nehemiah 12:9.
A porter keeping watch of the store house of the gates (Nehemiah 12:25).
Bakkukedit

See Bakbuk

Baniedit

Bani (בָּנִי "my son") was the name of 16 individuals in the Hebrew Bible.

A Gadite and one of David's mighty men (2 Samuel 23:36).
A Levite, whose son was appointed to service at the tabernacle at David's rule (1 Chronicles 6:46).
A Judahite whose son lived in Jerusalem after the exile (1 Chronicles 9:4).
See Binnui
One who took a strange wife, along with his brothers being the son of Bani (Ezra 10:34,38).
Son of Bani, a Levite and builder (Nehemiah 6:17).
Instructed the people in Ezra's time (Nehemiah 8:7).
Three Levites mentioned in connection with temple worship at Ezra's time (Nehemiah 9:4,5).
A Levite who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:13).
A leader of a people who also signed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:14).
The father of Uzzi who led as an overseer in Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:22).
Baracheledit

Barachel (בָּרַכְאֵל "God blesses")[148] was a Buzite, and was the father of Elihu, an antagonist of Job, according to Job 32:2.

Bariahedit

Bariah (בָּרִיחַ "fleeing" or "fugitive") was a descendant of the royal family of Judah, being one of the three sons of Shemaiah (1 Chronicles 3:22).

Barkosedit

Barkos (בַּרְקוֹס) was a painter who was the father of some of the Nethinim, and head of a family of temple-slaves who returned from exile with Zerubbabel according to Ezra 2:53.

Baruchedit
See also: Baruch ben Neriah

Baruch was the name of 3 minor biblical individuals.

A priest, the son of Zabbai, who helped in rebuilding the Wall of Jerusalem (Nehemiah 3:20).
A priest who signed the covenant with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:6).
The son of Col-hozeh, a descendant of Pharez of the tribe of Judah (Nehemiah 11:5).
Barzillaiedit
"Barzillai" redirects here. For the given name, see Barzillai (given name).

Barzillai [ברזלי "Iron-like"] was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

The Gileadite of Rogelim was 80 years old at the time of Absalom's revolt against King David. Barzillai supplied provisions for David's army at Mahanaim (2 Samuel 17:27–29). After the death of Absalom, being an old man, he was unable to accompany the king back to Jerusalem, but brought Chimham to David for the return journey (2 Samuel 19:31–37).
Another figure who married one of Barzillai's daughters was called Barzellai as a result (Ezra 2:61; Nehemiah 7:63). In 1 Esdras 5:38, he is called Zorzelleus.
Basemathedit

Hebrew: Sweet-smelling or Sweet-smile

Basemath, wife of Esau, and daughter of Elon the Hittite (Genesis 26:34). She is thought to be identical to or a sister to Adah who is mentioned in Genesis 36.[149]
Basemath, another wife of Esau, daughter of Ishmael, sister to Nebajoth and mother of Reuel (Genesis 36:3). She is thought by some scholars to be the same as Mahalath of Genesis 28.
Basemath, the daughter of Solomon; a wife of Ahimaaz. (1 Kings 4:15)
Bavaiedit

Bavai (bawway; Septuagint Codex Alexandrinus, Benei; Codex Vaticanus, Bedei; the King James Version Bavai, "wisher"), was mentioned as one of those who helped rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem.[150]

Bazlithedit

Bazlith (בַצְלִית) or Bazluth (בַּצְלוּת) was the ancestor whose descendants were among the Nethinim, and returned with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 7:54; Ezra 2:52)

Bazluthedit

See Bazlith[151]

Bealiahedit

Bealiah (בְּעַלְיָה, Be‘alyah) or Baalyah, a Benjamite, was one of David's thirty heroes who went to Ziklag, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12:5. The name derives from Baal and Jah, and according to the International Standard Bible Encyclopedia (1915) means "Yahweh is Lord."[152]

Bebaiedit

Bebai (בֵּבַי) was the name of 3 biblical individuals.

Ancestor of those who returned with Ezra, to Jerusalem (Ezra 8:11). His descendants were 623 which returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:11). Nehemiah 7:6, gives the number of 628. Most of his descendants married foreign wives (Ezra 10:28).
Father of Zechariah and a descendant of Bebai (Ezra 8:11).
Chief of the people who signed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:15).
Becheredit

Becher (בֶכֶר)[153] was the name of two individuals mentioned in the Bible:

The second of ten sons of Benjamin according to Genesis 46:21 and 1 Chronicles 7:6
A son of Ephraim according to Numbers 26:35. His descendants were referred to as Bachrites.
Bechorathedit

Becorath (בְּכוֹרַת "first-born"),[154] son of Aphiah, of the tribe of Benjamin, was an ancestor of King Saul and of his commander Abner. According to Saul, his family was the least of the tribe of Benjamin. (1 Samuel 9)

Becorathedit

See Bechorath

Bedadedit

Bedad (בְּדַד "solitary")[155] was the father of Hadad of Edom, (Genesis 36:35). In 1 Chronicles 1:46, either he, his son or both defeated the Midianites in Moab and their city was named Avith.

Bedanedit

Bedan (בְּדָן "in judging")[156] was the name of 2 biblical figures.

One of the leaders of Israel, mentioned along with Gideon, Jephthah and Samuel who was commemorated as one of the deliverers of the nation (1 Samuel 12:11). It is likely that the text refers to Barak in the Septuagint, Syriac and Arabic.[157]
One of the sons of Ulam of the tribe of Manasseh (1 Chronicles 7:17).
Bedeiahedit

Bedeiah (בֵּדְיָה "servant of YHWH"),[158] an Israelite exile, is a descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife (Ezra 10:35).

Beeraedit

Beera (בְּאֵרָא "a well") was a son of Zophah and from the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:37).

Beerahedit

Beerah (בְּאֵרָה "well")[159] was one of the princes of Reuben whom Tiglath-Pileser III carried away to Assyria (1 Chronicles 5:6). He was the son of Baal.

Beeriedit

Beeri (בְּאֵרִי "my well")[160] was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

The father of the prophet Hosea (Hosea 1:1). Jewish tradition says that he only uttered a few words of prophecy, and as they were insufficient to be embodied in a book by themselves, they were incorporated in the Book of Isaiah, viz., verses 19 and 20 of the 8th chapter. As such, Beeri is considered a prophet in Judaism.[161]
The Hittite father of Judith wife of Esau (Genesis 26:34).
Bekeredit

See Becher.

Belaedit

Hebrew: בלע BeLa' "Crooked"

Bela was the name of three individuals mentioned in the Bible:

Bela ben Beor, an Edomite king according to Genesis 36:32 and 1 Chronicles 1:43
(also "Belah") The first of ten sons of Benjamin according to Genesis 46:21, Numbers 26:38, and 1 Chronicles 7 and 8.
A son of Azaz according to 1 Chronicles 5:8
Belahedit

See Bela

Benedit

See Jaaziel

Ben Abinadabedit

Ben Abinadab (Hebrew בנ אבינדב BeN ,'aḄYNaDaḄ "My Father is Liberal"), was one of King Solomon's twelve regional administrators; he was over Dor, and he was married to Taphath, a daughter of Solomon. 1 Kings 4:11 (RSV).

Ben-Ammiedit

Ben-Ammi (Hebrew בן־עמי for "son of my people"[162]) was the son of Lot and his youngest daughter. He became the father of the Ammonites (see Genesis 19:36–38).

Ben Dekeredit

Ben Dekar (Hebrew בנ דקר BeN DeQeR "Son of Pick"), was one of King Solomon's twelve regional administrators; he was over Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan. 1 Kings 4:9 (RSV).

Ben Geberedit

Ben Geber (Hebrew בנ גבר BeN GeḄeR "Son of He-Man"), was one of King Solomon's twelve regional administrators; he was responsible for Ramoth-Gilead and Argob (1 Kings 4:13).

Ben-hailedit

Ben-hail (Hebrew: Ben-Cha'yil, בֶּןאּחִיַל, son of strength, i.e. warrior; Sept. translates οἱ υἱοὶ τῶν δυνατῶν), was one of the princes sent by king Jehoshaphat throughout the Kingdom of Judah, as to fulfill the king's reformation.

Ben-hananedit

Ben-hanan (בֶּן־חָנָן "son of favor") was the son of Shimon in the line of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:20).

Ben Hesededit

Ben Hesed (Hebrew בנ חסד ben hesed "Son of Grace"), was one of King Solomon's twelve regional administrators; he was over Aruboth, Sochoh, and Hepher. 1 Kings 4:10 (RSV).

Ben Huredit

Ben Hur (Hebrew בנ חור Ben Hur "Son of Hur") was one of King Solomon's twelve regional administrators; he was over Ephraim. 1 Kings 4:8 (RSV).

Ben-Zohethedit

Ben-Zoheth (בֶּן־זוֹחֵת "son of Zoheth") was a descendant of Judah being a descendant of Ishi (1 Chronicles 4:20).

Benaiahedit

Benaiah was the name of 12 minor biblical individuals.

A Pirathonite, and one of David's mighty men who was chief of the course in the 11th month, numbering 24,000 (2 Samuel 23:30; 1 Chronicles 11:31; 27:14).
Chief over the house of Simeon (1 Chronicles 4:36).
A Levite appointed as a singer with "psalteries set to Alamoth" (1 Chronicles 15:18,20; 16:5).
A priest who was appointed by Yahweh to blow the trumpet before the Ark of the Covenant (1 Chronicles 15:24; 16:6).
The father of Jehoiada (1 Chronicles 27:34). Possibly the same as the prominent Benaiah.
An ancestor of Jahaziel of the house of Asaph (2 Chronicles 20:14).
An overseer in the service of Hezekiah (2 Chronicles 31:13).
Four different men who married foreign wives (Ezra 10:25,30,35,43).
The father of Pelatiah seen in the visions of Ezekiel the prophet (Ezekiel 11:1,3).
Beninuedit

Beninu (בְּנִינוּ "our son")[163] was a returning Levite exile who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 10:13–14).

Benjaminedit

Benjamin was the name of 2 minor biblical individuals.

A Benjamite being the son of Bilhan, and the head of the family of warriors (1 Chronicles 7:10).
One of the sons of Harim, who married a foreign wife (Ezra 10:32).
Benoedit

Beno was the son of Merari and from Jaaziah 1 Chronicles 24:26–27.

Beoredit
See also: Beor (biblical figure)

Beor was the name of 2 biblical figures.

The father of king Bela of Edom who was one of the kings of Edom who reigned "before there reigned any king over the children of Israel" (Genesis 36:31–32; 1 Chronicles 1:43).
The father of Balaam who in Jewish Tradition is venerated as a prophet (Numbers 22–24; 31:8; Joshua 13:22).[164] He and other men who were fathers of notable prophets is also mentioned and commemorated.
Berachahedit

Berachah (בְּרָכָה "blessing") was one of the Benjamite warriors who joined David in Ziklag (1 Chronicles 12:3).

Beraiahedit

Beraiah (בְּרָאיָה "YHWH has created")[165] was the son of Shimhi, chief man of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:21).

Berechiahedit

Berechiah was the name of 7 biblical figures.

The father of the prophet Zechariah and son of Iddo (Zechariah 1:1; 11:7). Also called Jeberechiah or Jeberekiah in Isaiah 8:2.
One of the sons of Zerubbabel (1 Chronicles 3:19–20).
The father of Asaph the seer (1 Chronicles 6:39; 15:17).
An inhabitant of Jerusalem and a Levite (1 Chronicles 9:16)
The doorkeeper for the ark in David's time (1 Chronicles 15:23).
One of the heads of the tribe of Ephraim (2 Chronicles 28:12).
The father of Meshullam the builder during Nehemiah's time (Nehemiah 3:4,30; 6:18).
Beriahedit

Beriah is the name of four different biblical individuals:

One of Asher's four sons, and father of Heber and Malchiel.[166]
A son of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:20–23), born after the killing of Ephraim's sons Ezer and Elead, and so called by his father "because disaster had befallen his house."[167] He was the father of Rephah, the ancestor of Joshua son of Nun son of Elishama.
A Benjamite, son of Elpaal. He and his brother Shema expelled the Gittites, and were patriarchs to the inhabitants of Ajalon. His sons were Michael, Ishpah and Joha. (1 Chr. 8:13)
A Levite, the son of Shimei. He was jointly patriarch of a clan with his brother Jeush. (1 Chr. 23:10–11)
Berededit

Bered (בֶּרֶד "hail")[168] was the son of Shulethah, being the grandson of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20).

Beriedit

Beri (בֵּרִי "a well")[169] was the son of Zophah of the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:36).

Besaiedit

Besai (בֵּסַי "my treading")[170] was the ancestor of the Nethinim who returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem (Ezra 2:49; Nehemiah 7:52).

Besodeiahedit

Besodeiah (בְּסוֹדְיָה "with the counsel of YHWH" or "in the secret of the Lord")[171] was the father of another Meshullam, who was another builder of the wall of Jerusalem in the time of Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:6).

Beth-raphaedit

Beth-rapha (בֵּית רָפָא "house of healing") was a descendant of Judah being the son of Eshton (1 Chronicles 4:12).

Bethueledit
Main article: Bethuel

Bethuel was the youngest son of Nahor and Milcah. Nephew of Abraham and father of Rebecca and Laban (Genesis 22:21–23).

Beth Zuredit

Beth Zur (בֵּית צוּר "house of the rock")[172] is mentioned in (1 Chr. 2:45) as the son of Maon the son of Shammai. He is also a Jerahmeelite.

Bezaiedit

Bezai (בֵּצַי) was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

A chief who sealed the covenant (Nehemiah 10:18).
His 323 descendants (Nehemiah 7:23) or 324 (Ezra 2:17) returned with Zerubbabel to Jerusalem.
Bezaleledit

Bezalel (בְּצַלְאֵל)[173] was an architect who constructed the ark in connection with the tabernacle in the wilderness, he was engaged principally in works of metal, wood, and stone; while Aholiab, who was associated with him and subordinate to him, had the charge of the textile fabrics (Exodus 31:2; 35:30; 36:1–2; 38:22).

Bezaleeledit

Bezaleel (בְּצַלְאֵל) was one of the descendants of Pahath-Moab guilty of intermarriage (Ezra 10:30).

Bezeredit

Bezer (בֶּצֶר "gold ore" or "remote fortress")[174] was from the tribe of Asher being the son of Zophah (1 Chronicles 7:37).

Bichriedit

Bichri (בִּכְרִי "youthful")[175] was a Benjamite being the father of Sheba who led an insurrection against king David; whom Joab and his army pursued and lob his head over the town's wall (2 Samuel 20:1).

Bidkaredit

Bidkar (Hebrew: בדקר) was an officer of the Israelite king Jehu. Jehu ordered Bidkar to throw the body of the king he usurped, Jehoram, into the field of Naboth, fulfilling prophecy. 2 Kings 9:25

Bigthaedit

See Biztha

Bigthanaedit

Bigthana (Hebrew: בִּגְתָן, בִּגְתָנָא Bīgṯān, Bīgṯānāʾ) was a eunuch of king Ahasuerus who in the Greek Septuagint translation of the Bible, they were known as Gabatha (Koine Greek: Γαβαθά καὶ Θαρρα). Bigthan's name is also spelled "Bigtan" or "Bigthana". It is a Persian name which means "Gift of God".[176] He and Theresh were planning to kill the king whom Mordecai warned Ahasuerus of.

Bigvaiedit

The name Bigvai (בִּגְוַי) occurs several times in Ezra-Nehemiah (Ezra 2:2, 14, 8:14, Nehemiah 7:7, 19 and 10:16).[177] That refers to 3 people. In the last of these he is one of the "leaders of the people".[178] By 408 B.C. the Elephantine papyri show that Sanballat was the governor of Samaria, and Bigvai the governor of Jerusalem but Wright says that "it is not suggested that any of these [referred to in Ezra-Nehemiah] is the man who later became governor.[177]

Bilgahedit

Bilgah (בִּלְגַה) was allocated the fifteenth division of priestly service when lots were drawn in 1 Chronicles 24.

Bilhanedit

Bilhan (בִּלְהָן "their decrepitude")[179] was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

A Horite chief dwelling in Mount Seir, a descendant of Esau (Genesis 36:27; 1 Chronicles 1:42).
A Benjamite being the son of Jediael and father of Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish and Ahishahar (1 Chronicles 7:10).
Bilshanedit

Bilshan (בִּלְשָׁן), one of the important men who came with Zerubbabel from Babylon. (Ezra 2:2;Nehemiah 7:7) In 1 Esdras 5:8 he is called Beelsarus. According to Rabbinical Literature, the name Bilshan is improper, but a surname to the preceding name Mordecai. The latter was given this epithet because of his linguistic attainments.[180]

Bimhaledit

Bimhal (בִּמְהָל) was one of the sons of Japhlet in the tribe of Asher (1 Chronicles 7:33).

Bineaedit

Binea (בִּנְעָא "fountain"),[181] a descendant of Jonathan, was the son of Moza and the father of Rephaiah or Rapha. He is mentioned in two passages: 1 Chronicles 8:37 and 1 Chronicles 9:43.

Binnuiedit

Binnui (בִּנּוּי) was the name of 4 biblical individuals.

A Levite, father of Noadiah and living in the time of Ezra (Ezra 8:33; Nehemiah 12:8).
One of the descendants of Pahath-Moab guilty of intermarriage and Balnuus of 1 Esdras 9:31 (Ezra 10:30). He was also called Bani who was also mentioned being intermarried (Ezra 10:38).
The son of Henadad who built the part of wall of Jerusalem; he also sealed the covenant with Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:24; 10:9). He is identical with Bavvai son of Henadad mentioned in Nehemiah 3:18 which is either a corrupt version of Binnui. Or is a Levitical house which Bavvai was a chief. Nehemiah 10:9 supports this theory as Binnui is a leader and besides, the names in these verses are obviously of priests and Levites.
One of the heads who went with Zerubbabel (Nehemiah 7:15; Ezra 2:10).
Birshaedit

Birsha (בִּרְשַׁע) is the king of Gomorrah in Genesis 14 who joins other Canaanite city kings in rebelling against Chedorlaomer.

Bishlamedit

Bishlam was one of the three foreign colonists who wrote a complaint letter concerning the Jews to Artaxerxes (Ezra 4:7). The Septuagint renders Bishlam as ἐν εἰρήνῃ (en eirēnē), "in peace", as though it were a phrase rather than a proper name; this is clearly or possibly an error.[182] In 1 Esdras, his name is given as Belemus.[183]

Bizthaedit

Biztha was the second of the seven eunuchs of Ahasuerus; it may be possible that the name is derived from the Persian besteh, "bound," hence, "eunuch" (Esther 1:10).

Bocheruedit

Bocheru (בֹּכְרוּ "firstborn"),[184] a Benjamite, was one of the 6 sons of Azel. He is mentioned two times in the Hebrew Bible: 1 Chronicles 8:38 and 1 Chronicles 9:44.

Bohanedit

Bohan (בֹּהַן "thumb") was mentioned in Joshua 15:6; 18:17 as whose stone served as a boundary mark from Judah to Benjamin. He is neither mentioned in the lists of Reuben's sons. Some suggest he was the one who set that rock.[185]

Bukkiedit

Bukki (בֻּקִּי) was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

A prince of the tribe of Dan, son of Jogli; one of those appointed by Moses to superintend the division of Canaan amongst the tribe (Num. 34:22).
A son of Abishua, father of Uzzi, and a priest from the line of Aaron (1 Chronicles 6:5,51; Ezra 7:4).
Bukkiahedit

Bukkiah (בֻּקִּיָּה "YHWH has emptied")[186] was a Kohathite Levite being one of the sons of Heman one of the musicians of the first temple (1 Chronicles 25:4,13).

Bunahedit

Bunah (בּוּנָה "intelligence")[187] is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:25 as a son of Jerahmeel, a Judahite.

Bunniedit

Bunni (בֻּנִּי) was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

A Levite living in the time of described as "Standing on the stairs of the Levites were" (Nehemiah 9:4).
The father of Hashabiah whose descendant, Shemaiah the Levite inhabited the newly recovered city Jerusalem (Nehemiah 11:15).
Buzedit

Buz (בּוּז) was the name of 2 biblical individuals.

The second son of Nahor and Milcah (Genesis 22:21). Elihu, the Book of Job's antagonist was his prominent descendant (Job 32:2).
One of the chiefs of the tribe of Gad (1 Chronicles 5:14).
Buziedit

Buzi (Hebrew: בּוּזִי, Būzī) was the father of Ezekiel and priest of Jerusalem (Ezekiel 1:3). Ezekiel, like Jeremiah, is said to have been a descendant of Joshua by his marriage with the proselyte Rahab (Talmud Meg. 14b; Midrash Sifre, Num. 78).

Calcoledit

See Chalcol

Calebedit
See also: Caleb (son of Hezron)

This is about the Caleb mentioned only in 1 Chronicles 2:18. For the better-known Caleb son of Jephunneh, see Caleb.

Canaanitish Womanedit

The Canaanitish Woman can refer to one unnamed biblical individual.

The mother of Shaul, son of Simeon. She was a Canaanite of Canaan whom Simeon was married to, it is unclear whether she was the mother of the other sons of Simeon (Genesis 46:10; Exodus 6:15).
Carkasedit

Carkas or Carcas is one of the seven eunuchs whom Ahasuerus summoned to parade queen Vashti (Esther 1:10).

Carmiedit

Carmi (כַּרְמִי "my vineyard")[188] refers to two individuals mentioned in the Bible:

The fourth son of Reuben and progenitor of the Carmites according to Genesis 46:9, Numbers 26:6, and 1 Chronicles 5:3.
The son of Zabdi, grandson of Zerah of the Tribe of Judah, and the father of Achan, according to Joshua 7:1. He was present at the Battle of Jericho.
Carshenaedit

Carshena or Karshena is a name which appears in a list of high-ranking officials of Persia and Media in the court of king Ahasuerus in Esther 1:14. It is derived from the Persian warkačīnā, meaning "wolfish".[189]

Chalcoledit

Chalcol, the brother of Darda (Hebrew כלכל kalkol – the same consonants with different vowel points (kilkayl) mean "maintain") is listed in 1 Kings 4:31 as an example of a very wise man who is, nevertheless, not as wise as Solomon. Another person with the same Hebrew name (though spelled Calcol in the King James Version) is listed in 1 Chronicles as the son of Zerah, the son of Judah (son of Jacob).[190]

Chelaledit

See Kelal.

Chelluhedit

Chelluh, Cheluhi, or Cheluhu (כְּלוּהַי "my accomplishment") is the name given in Ezra 10:35 for one of the men who married foreign women.[191]

Chelubedit

Two individuals by the name of Chelub (כְּלוּב "caged")[192] are mentioned in the Hebrew Bible.

A descendant of Judah, called "brother of Shuhah" in 1 Chronicles 4:11, in a genealogical passage listing descendants of Judah. According to the Encyclopaedia Biblica (1899), this "Chelub" is the biblical figure better known as Caleb.[193]
An Ezri son of Chelub was an overseer of agricultural work in the time of king David according to 1 Chronicles 27:26.
Chelubaiedit

See #Caleb

Chesededit

See Kesed

Chenaanahedit

Chenaanah (Hebrew:כְּנַעֲנָה "trader") is the name of two biblical figures.

In a genealogical section of Chronicles concerned with the Tribe of Benjamin, a Chenaanah son of Bilhan is mentioned.[194]
The false prophet Zedekiah is called "son of Chenaanah".[195]
Chenaniedit

Chenani (כְּנָנִי "my station")[196] was one of the men mentioned in Nehemiah 9:4, in connection with the constitution of "congregation." If the names represent houses or families, eight Levitical houses probably sang some well-known psalm on this occasion.

Chenaniahedit

Chenaniah (כְּנַנְיָה), according to Chronicles, was a Levite leader in the time of David.[197] The Hebrew text is unclear as to whether he was in charge of something to do with singing or with the carrying of the ark.[198]

Cheranedit

Cheran or Keran (כְּרָן "lyre"),[199] an Edomite, was the son of Dishon the Horite duke (Genesis 36:26; 1 Chronicles 1:41).

He was David's son with his third wife Abigail, widow of Nabal the Carmelite, and is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 3:1, and 2 Samuel 3:3. Unlike the other of David's three elder sons, Amnon, Absalom, and Adonijah who were important characters in 2 Samuel, Chileab is only named in the list of David's sons and no further mention is made of him. Chimhamedit

Chimham, Chimhan [200] or Kimham [201] (כִּמְהָם "their longing")[202] was a servant nominated by Barzillai to accompany King David to Gilgal during his return to Jerusalem from beyond the Jordan after the death of Absalom. (2 Samuel 19:37–40)

The name also refers to a place near Bethlehem where Johanan regrouped before departing to Egypt.[203]

Chislonedit

Chislon (Hebrew: כִּסְלוֹן "confidence") was the father of Elidad, a prince of the Tribe of Benjamin. (Num. 34:21)

Col-hozehedit

Col-hozeh (כׇּל־חֹזֶה "all-seeing")[204] was the father of Shallum (Nehemiah 3:15), who was the official of Mizpah at the time, and head of the repairs to certain walls and fountains. He is further mentioned as the father of Baruch though it is not explicitly mentioned that Baruch's brother was Shallum, distinguishing this Col-hozeh from the previous (Nehemiah 11:5).

Conaniahedit

Conaniah, also Konaniah, (כּוֹנַנְיָהוּ "YHWH has established")[205] was the name of two individuals:

a Levite appointed with his brother, Shimei, by Hezekiah and Azariah the priest, to be the overseer to the tithes to the temple (2 Chronicles 31:12–13)
a later Levite placed over the tithes in the time of Josiah (2 Chronicles 35:9).
Concubine, Aramitessedit

The concubine, Aramitess was the mother of Machir, the father of Gilead, she was the concubine of Ashriel (1 Chronicles 7:14).

Cozedit

Coz or Koz (קוֹץ) was the son of Helah and father of Anub and Hazzobebah (1 Chronicles 4:8).

Cushiedit

Cushi (כּוּשִׁי) was the name of 2 biblical individuals found in the Hebrew Bible.

The father of Shelemiah, and so as the great-grandfather of Jehudi who later joined Jeremiah and Baruch in the request of the men to read the scrolls of Jeremiah to the king's direct advisors. Some point afterwards, Jehoiachim demolishes the scroll by casting it to a pit of fire. (Jeremiah 36:14)
The father of the Prophet Zephaniah in Zephaniah 1:1; he was also the son of Gedaliah which was the son of Amariah the son of Hezekiah.

Another unnamed biblical figure called "the Cushite" is found in 2 Samuel 18:21 as a messenger from Joab who brought tidings to David, after the death of Absalom whom Joab killed. Shortly after David mourns for his beloved son. (2 Samuel 18:21–32) The King James Version translates his name as Cushi as a term for an Ethiopian descent.

Dathanedit

Dathan along with Korah and Abiram, being the son of Eliab rebelled against Moses (Numbers 16:1). He was sent to Sheol by Yahweh cause of his disobedience (Numbers 26:9).

Daughter of Machiredit

The Daughter of Machir was an unnamed biblical figure mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:21, she was the daughter of Machir the son of Manasseh and one of the wives of Hezron who bore him Segub which became the father of Jair.

Daughter of Meshullamedit

The Daughter of Meshullam is an unnamed biblical individual whom Johanan, Tobiah's son married; her father was Meshullam (Nehemiah 6:18).

Daughter of Putieledit

The Daughter of Putiel is an unnamed biblical individual whom Eleazar the son of Aaron married and bore him Phinehas (Exodus 6:25).

Daughter of Shechaniahedit

The Daughter of Shechaniah is a biblical figure unnamed and married to Tobiah, she was daughter to Shechaniah son of Arah, whom her father was widely respected; affecting her husband as feared (Nehemiah 6:18).

Daughter of Shuahedit

The Daughter of Shuah is an unnamed figure married to Judah, son of Jacob; she was the daughter of Shuah who bore Judah, Er, Onan and Shelah (Genesis 38:2). The reference to Judah's wife in Genesis 38:12 refers to her as the "daughter of Shuah", or "bat-Shuah" in Hebrew. This has led some to take Bat-Shuah (and variants) as her actual name.[208] A midrashic tradition says her name was Aliyath.[209] Bat-Shuah is also an alternative name for Bathsheba, wife of Judah's descendant, King David.[210]

Debiredit

Debir was a king of Eglon, slain by Joshua and his valiant men, he camped before Gibeon and warred against it with the other kings, they hid in a cave and was hunged later (Joshua 18:1–26).

Deborahedit

Deborah appears in the Hebrew Bible as the wet nurse of Rebecca (Genesis 35:8). She is first mentioned by name in the Torah when she dies in a place called Alon Bachot (אלון בכות), "Tree of Weepings" (Genesis 35:8), and is buried by Jacob, who is returning with his large family to Canaan. According to Rashi, Deborah was sent by Laban to care for his sister Rebecca when the latter went to marry Isaac (Genesis 24:59).

Dedanedit

Dedan (Hebrew:דְּדָן‎) may refer to 2 biblical characters.

A son of Raamah, son of Cush the son of Ham (Genesis 10:7; 1 Chronicles 1:9). His descendants is further mentioned in Isaiah 21:13, Ezekiel 27:15. They probably settled among the sons of Cush, on the northwest coast of the Persian Gulf (aka Arabian Gulf) and their descendants are likely among the Arabs of today.
The son of Jokshan, the son of Abraham through Keturah and his sons, Leummim, Letushim and Asshurim (Genesis 25:3; 1 Chronicles 1:32).

The head of a family that came up from the Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel, that was unable to give its ancestral genealogy. (Ezr. 2:60, Neh. 7:62)
One of the sons of Elioenai, a descendant of the royal Davidic line through Jeconiah. (1 Chronicles 3:24). He lived after the exile and was a descendant of Zerubbabel as a 3x great-grandson.
Son of Mehetabel and father of Shemaiah. (Neh. 6:10)

Elnathanedit

Elnathan (Hebrew אלנתן Elnathan "God gave") is a Hebrew name found in 2 Kings, Jeremiah and Ezra.

According to 2 Kings 24:8, Elnathan of Jerusalem was the father of Nehushta. Nehushta was the mother of King Jeconiah, whose father was King Jehoiakim. Despite this close relationship to the king, Elnathan was one of those who, according to Jeremiah 36:25 opposed Jehoiakim when he cut up and burnt a scroll that had been brought to him, containing Jeremiah's prophesies of the forthcoming destruction of Judah. Elnathan's father Achbor was a strong supporter of the earlier reforms of King Josiah, which may have influenced Elnathan's behavior,[231] although according to Jeremiah 26:20–23 he had earlier been closely involved in the persecution of the prophet Uriah ben Shemaiah.

In Ezra 8:16, the name Elnathan occurs three times:

Then sent I for Eliezer, for Ariel, for Shemaiah, and for Elnathan, and for Jarib, and for Elnathan, and for Nathan, and for Zechariah, and for Meshullam, chief men; also for Joiarib, and for Elnathan, which were teachers. (Revised Version)

Donna Laird proposes that the repetition of "Elnathan", and the similarity between the names "Jarib" and "Joiarib", indicate a copyist's accidental repetition.[232]

Ephronedit

Ephron the Hittite, son of Zohar, lived in Mamre among the children of Heth. Abraham came to the Hittites, who were strangers to him, and asked them to sell him a property that he could use as a burial site for Sarah, his wife. The Hittites, flattering Abraham by calling him a mighty prince, said that he could choose whichever tomb he wanted.[239] Abraham then asked his hosts to contact Ephron, son of Zohar, who owned a field where the cave of Machpelah was located, which he was offering to buy for "the full price". Ephron slyly replies that he is prepared to give Abraham the field and the cave within, knowing that that would not result in Abraham having a permanent claim on it.[240] Abraham politely refuses the offer and insists on paying for the field. Ephron replies that the field is worth four hundred shekels of silver, and Abraham agrees to the price without any further bargaining.[240] He then proceeded to bury Sarah there.[241]

**Arijit Singh**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-2) (Bengali pronunciation:[[ɔɾid͡ʒit̪ʃiŋɦo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali"); born 25 April 1987) is an [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people")[singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Singer "Singer"), [composer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composer "Composer"), and [music producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_producer "Music producer"). He has been described by critics as one of the most influential and commercially successful vocalists in Indian music, and is noted for his emotive vocal style and work across multiple genres.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-3)

He has received two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer") and eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer"). In 2025, he received the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), one of India’s highest civilian honours, for his contributions to the arts.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-4)

Singh began his career in 2005 as a contestant on the reality television programme _[Fame Gurukul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fame\_Gurukul "Fame Gurukul")_. He subsequently worked as a music programmer and assistant to composers including [Pritam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam "Pritam") before making his playback singing debut in Hindi cinema with “Phir Mohabbat” (2011). He gained wider recognition in 2013 with “[Tum Hi Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tum_Hi_Ho "Tum Hi Ho")” from _[Aashiqui 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashiqui\_2 "Aashiqui 2"),_ which earned him his first Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-5)

In 2025, he received his eighth Filmfare Award for “[Sajni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sajni_(song) "Sajni (song)")”, equalling [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar")’s record for the most wins in the Best Male Playback Singer category.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-7)

Singh has been the most-streamed artist on [Spotify](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spotify "Spotify") in India for seven consecutive years, from 2019 to 2025.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-8)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Singh was born on 25 April 1987[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-9) in [Jiaganj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jiaganj "Jiaganj"), [Murshidabad district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murshidabad_district "Murshidabad district"), [West Bengal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Bengal "West Bengal"), India, to Surinder Kakkar Singh, a [Punjabi Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Sikh "Punjabi Sikh") father,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-lj-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-kg-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-fc-12) and Aditi Singh, a [Bengali Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Hindu "Bengali Hindu") mother.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-public_transport-13) His paternal family migrated from [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore") during the [Partition of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-lj-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-kg-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-fc-12)

Singh was raised in a musically inclined family and began training in music at an early age. His maternal aunt was trained in [Indian classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_classical_music "Indian classical music"), while his maternal grandmother sang. His maternal uncle played the [tabla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabla "Tabla"), and his mother also sang and played the instrument.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-public_transport-13)

He attended [Raja Bijay Singh High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murshidabad#Educational_Institutes "Murshidabad") and later studied at Sripat Singh College, affiliated with the [University of Kalyani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Kalyani "University of Kalyani").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-public_transport-13) He has stated that he was a “decent student” but was more inclined towards music,leading his parents to arrange formal training.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-public_transport-13)

He received training in [Indian classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_classical_music "Indian classical music") from Rajendra Prasad Hazari and in tabla from Dhirendra Prasad Hazari. He was also trained in [Rabindra Sangeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindra_Sangeet "Rabindra Sangeet") and Western pop music by Birendra Prasad Hazari.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-public_transport-13) He began training under the Hazari brothers at the age of three, and at the age of nine received a government scholarship for vocal training in Indian classical music.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-mess-14)

Growing up, he listened to composers such as [Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Amadeus_Mozart "Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart") and [Ludwig van Beethoven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludwig_van_Beethoven "Ludwig van Beethoven"), as well as [modern Bengali music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_music "Bengali music").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-15) He has cited musicians including [Bade Ghulam Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade_Ghulam_Ali_Khan "Bade Ghulam Ali Khan"), [Ustad Rashid Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ustad_Rashid_Khan "Ustad Rashid Khan"), [Zakir Hussain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zakir_Hussain_(musician) "Zakir Hussain (musician)"), and Anand Chatterjee as influences, and has also expressed admiration for singers such as [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), [Hemant Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemant_Kumar "Hemant Kumar"), and [Manna Dey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manna_Dey "Manna Dey").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-film-16)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Early career and breakthrough

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early career and breakthrough")]

In the early 2010s, Singh began receiving opportunities in film music, frequently collaborating with [Pritam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam "Pritam") on film soundtracks including _[Golmaal 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golmaal\_3 "Golmaal 3")_, _[Crook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crook\_(film) "Crook (film)")_, and _[Action Replayy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action\_Replayy "Action Replayy")_. He also recorded "Neeve Na Neeve Na" for the Telugu film _[Kedi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kedi\_(2010\_film) "Kedi (2010 film)")_ and made his Hindi playback debut with "Phir Mohabbat" from _[Murder 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder\_2 "Murder 2")_.

He gained industry recognition with "Raabta" from _[Agent Vinod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agent\_Vinod\_(2012\_film) "Agent Vinod (2012 film)")_ (2012), and subsequently contributed to the soundtracks of films such as _[Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Players\_(2012\_film) "Players (2012 film)")_, _[Cocktail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocktail\_(2012\_film) "Cocktail (2012 film)")_, and _[Barfi!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barfi!\_(2012\_film) "Barfi! (2012 film)")_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-CocktailReview-17)

His breakthrough came with _[Aashiqui 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashiqui\_2 "Aashiqui 2")_ (2013), particularly the song "[Tum Hi Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tum_Hi_Ho "Tum Hi Ho")", which achieved commercial success and earned him the [Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer"). The song is considered a turning point in his career.

Following this, he recorded songs for films including _[Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Jawaani\_Hai\_Deewani "Yeh Jawaani Hai Deewani")_, _[Chennai Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai\_Express "Chennai Express")_, _[Jackpot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackpot\_(2013\_film) "Jackpot (2013 film)")_, and _[Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goliyon\_Ki\_Raasleela\_Ram-Leela "Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela")_, further establishing his presence in Hindi film music.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-RamLeelaInterview-18)

### 2014–2019: Continued success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2014–2019: Continued success")]

During the mid-2010s, Singh remained a prominent figure in Indian film music, collaborating frequently with composers such as [Pritam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam "Pritam") and [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar").

In 2019, he recorded "Khairiyat" for the film _[Chhichhore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhichhore "Chhichhore")_, composed by Pritam with lyrics by [Amitabh Bhattacharya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bhattacharya "Amitabh Bhattacharya"); the song achieved commercial success and streaming popularity. In the same year, he recorded "[Tujhe Kitna Chahne Lage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tujhe_Kitna_Chahne_Lage "Tujhe Kitna Chahne Lage")" for _[Kabir Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir\_Singh "Kabir Singh")_, which was among the commercially successful Hindi film songs of the year.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_Kalank-19)

He also collaborated with [Shilpa Rao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shilpa_Rao "Shilpa Rao") on "[Ghungroo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghungroo_(song) "Ghungroo (song)")" from _[War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_(2019\_film) "War (2019 film)")_, composed by [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar") with lyrics by [Kumaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumaar "Kumaar").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-HT_War-20)

### 2020–present: Independent ventures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2020–present: Independent ventures")]

In 2020, Singh recorded songs for films including _[Love Aaj Kal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Aaj\_Kal\_(2020\_film) "Love Aaj Kal (2020 film)")_, _[Chhapaak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhapaak "Chhapaak")_, _[Street Dancer 3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Street\_Dancer\_3D "Street Dancer 3D")_, and _[Malang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malang\_(film) "Malang (film)")_. During the COVID-19 pandemic, he also contributed to the soundtrack of the series _[The Forgotten Army – Azaadi Ke Liye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Forgotten\_Army\_%E2%80%93\_Azaadi\_Ke\_Liye "The Forgotten Army – Azaadi Ke Liye")_.

In July 2020, Singh launched his independent music label, Oriyon Music, marking a shift towards non-film music.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-OriyonLabel-21) He subsequently released non-film singles including “Dil Ko Maine Di Kasam”, composed by [Amaal Mallik](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amaal_Mallik "Amaal Mallik"), and “Rihaa”, his first independent single as singer, composer, and producer; a Bengali version titled “Mukto Kore Dao” was also released.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-IndependentSingles-22)

In 2022, he recorded "[Kesariya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesariya_(song) "Kesariya (song)")" from _[Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahm%C4%81stra:\_Part\_One\_%E2%80%93\_Shiva "Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva")_, for which he received the [Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer") at the 68th Filmfare Awards. In 2025, he received his eighth Filmfare Award for "[Sajni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sajni_(song) "Sajni (song)")" from _[Laapataa Ladies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laapataa\_Ladies "Laapataa Ladies")_, equalling [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar")’s record for the most wins in this category.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Filmfare2025-23)

Singh has remained among the most-streamed Indian artists on digital platforms throughout the 2020s, with his catalogue featuring in Spotify India year-end charts.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Spotify2024-24)

In October 2025, he provided uncredited vocals on the song "[Sapphire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sapphire_(song) "Sapphire (song)")" by [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), which was later included on his album [_Play_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Play_(Ed_Sheeran_album) "Play (Ed Sheeran album)") and subsequently featured on the remix of the track on the EP, _Play (The Remixes)_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-25)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-27)

In January 2026, he announced his retirement from playback singing, stating that he would no longer accept new assignments while continuing to pursue independent and classical music.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-28)

## Vocals and musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Vocals and musical style")]

Singh has been described as a [baritone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baritone "Baritone"), and is noted for his emotive vocal style and tonal quality.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-29) Critics have commented on the texture of his voice and its consistency in live performances.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Guardian2024-30) He has also been noted for his use of _[meend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meend "Meend")_ in his singing.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Guardian2024-30)

### Technical proficiency and training

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Technical proficiency and training")]

Singh's vocal training began at an early age under the Hazari brothers. He studied [Hindustani classical music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustani_classical_music "Hindustani classical music") under Rajendra Prasad Hazari, and was trained in [Rabindra Sangeet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindra_Sangeet "Rabindra Sangeet") and Western pop music by Birendra Prasad Hazari.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-DeccanChronicle2016-31)

His training has enabled him to perform across a range of vocal registers and musical styles.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-HansIndia2025-32) Critics have noted his use of techniques such as controlled voice modulation in his performances.

### Versatility and repertoire

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Versatility and repertoire")]

Singh is primarily associated with romantic ballads such as "[Tum Hi Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tum_Hi_Ho "Tum Hi Ho")" and "[Channa Mereya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channa_Mereya "Channa Mereya")", but has performed across multiple genres. His repertoire includes dance tracks such as "[Nashe Si Chadh Gayi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashe_Si_Chadh_Gayi "Nashe Si Chadh Gayi")", Punjabi folk-inspired songs including "[Samjhawan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samjhawan "Samjhawan")", and [Sufi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sufi_music "Sufi music")-influenced compositions such as "[Mast Magan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mast_Magan "Mast Magan")".[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-IndiaToday2026-33)

He has also recorded songs in electronic dance music and synth-pop, including "[Sooraj Dooba Hain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sooraj_Dooba_Hain "Sooraj Dooba Hain")" and "[Ghungroo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghungroo_(song) "Ghungroo (song)")".[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_RoyReview-34)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-HT_War-20)

He has collaborated with composers including [A. R. Rahman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A._R._Rahman "A. R. Rahman"), [Pritam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritam "Pritam"), and [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-ET_Journey-35)

## Public image and influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Public image and influences")]

### Musical influences

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Musical influences")]

Singh has cited a range of musical influences spanning Hindi film music, ghazal traditions, and contemporary international genres. He has acknowledged [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar") as a formative influence, particularly noting his versatility and vocal style.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-filmibeat-36)

He has also cited [Mohit Chauhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohit_Chauhan "Mohit Chauhan") and [Atif Aslam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atif_Aslam "Atif Aslam") among contemporary influences. Singh has described playback singer [KK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishnakumar_Kunnath "Krishnakumar Kunnath") as a significant artistic influence and has paid tribute to him in performances following his death.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_KK-37)

His musical influences also include ghazal artists such as [Ghulam Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghulam_Ali_(singer) "Ghulam Ali (singer)"), [Jagjit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jagjit_Singh "Jagjit Singh"), and [Mehdi Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehdi_Hassan "Mehdi Hassan"). He has expressed appreciation for international acts including [Coldplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coldplay "Coldplay") and has indicated interest in collaborating with artists such as [Norah Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norah_Jones "Norah Jones").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-IE_Ghazal-38)

### Public image

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Public image")]

Singh is known for maintaining a relatively low public profile despite his commercial success. Indian media have frequently characterised him as a “small-town” artist who rose to prominence in Hindi cinema from Jiaganj.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_Persona-39)

His limited media presence and infrequent television appearances, including a guest appearance on _[The Kapil Sharma Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kapil\_Sharma\_Show "The Kapil Sharma Show")_ in 2016, have been described as reflective of his reserved and private nature.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_Kapil-40)

He has stated that he previously avoided playing his own songs in his personal space in order to maintain a distinction between his professional work and private life.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_2026-41)

He has also stated that he engages minimally with social media and prefers that audience feedback be mediated through his team.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-AmarUjala-42)

### Industry commentary

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Industry commentary")]

In the 2020s, Singh commented on structural issues within the music industry, particularly concerning compensation practices for singers. In a 2023 interview, he criticised practices in which vocalists record songs without receiving adequate remuneration.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-43)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOI_2026-41)

## Impact and recognition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Impact and recognition")]

In 2025, he was awarded the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), India's fourth-highest civilian honour, for his contributions to the arts.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-HTPadma2025-44)

### Commercial and cultural impact

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Commercial and cultural impact")]

In 2025, his win for "[Sajni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sajni_(song) "Sajni (song)")" at the [70th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/70th_Filmfare_Awards "70th Filmfare Awards") marked his eighth [Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer"), equalling the record held by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar").[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-NewsBytesFilmfare2025-45)

His popularity has extended beyond the music industry, with public figures from other fields expressing admiration for his work. Cricketer [Virat Kohli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virat_Kohli "Virat Kohli") has described himself as a fan of Singh's music and praised his voice in media interactions.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-TOIKohli2026-46)

International publications have noted his global touring presence, including performances at venues such as London's [The O2 Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_O2_Arena "The O2 Arena").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Guardian2024-30) From 2019 to 2025, he remained the most-streamed artist in India for seven consecutive years.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-BStandard2025-47)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Family

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Family")]

Singh was born to a [Punjabi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabis "Punjabis")[Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") father, Surinder Kakkar Singh, and a [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal "Bengal")[Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindu "Hindu") mother, Aditi Singh.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Philanthropy-48) His mother, who influenced his early musical interests, died on 20 May 2021 at the age of 52 due to complications from a cerebral stroke.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-49)

In January 2014, Singh married Koel Roy in a private ceremony at [Tarapith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarapith "Tarapith"), West Bengal.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-50)

### Lifestyle and residence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Lifestyle and residence")]

Despite his prominence, Singh is known for maintaining a relatively low public profile. He resides primarily in his hometown of Jiaganj rather than [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). He is locally known by the nickname "Shomu" and has been reported to participate in community activities and use local modes of transport.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-51)

His residence has also been visited by public figures. In February 2025, British singer-songwriter [Ed Sheeran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran") visited Singh in Jiaganj, where they were seen travelling through the town together.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-52) This was followed by visits from Dutch DJ [Martin Garrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Garrix "Martin Garrix") in March 2025 and actor [Aamir Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamir_Khan "Aamir Khan") in February 2026 in connection with professional collaborations.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-AamirVisit-53)

### Philanthropy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Philanthropy")]

His initiatives are focused in the [Murshidabad district](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murshidabad_district "Murshidabad district"), where he has been associated with projects including a multi-specialty hospital, a music academy, and a sports complex.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Philanthropy-48)

### Interests

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Interests")]

Singh has expressed interest in sports, particularly badminton and football. He supports the English football club [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United "Manchester United") and has identified [Sachin Tendulkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachin_Tendulkar "Sachin Tendulkar"), [Sourav Ganguly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sourav_Ganguly "Sourav Ganguly"), and [Saina Nehwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saina_Nehwal "Saina Nehwal") among his favourite sportspersons.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Interests-54)

## Concerts, tours and events

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Concerts, tours and events")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Arijit_Singh_live_performance_at_Ovo_arena_Wembley_on_16_July_2016.jpg/250px-Arijit_Singh_live_performance_at_Ovo_arena_Wembley_on_16_July_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Arijit_Singh_live_performance_at_Ovo_arena_Wembley_on_16_July_2016.jpg)

Singh performing live at the [Wembley Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wembley_Arena "Wembley Arena") in London, July 2016.

### 2013–2015: Early career and international debut

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: 2013–2015: Early career and international debut")]

On 10 November 2013, he headlined the "Xpressions" festival at the Xavier Institute in Odisha.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-55)

In January 2015, Singh made an international appearance in Dubai accompanied by a 50-piece Grand Symphony Orchestra from London.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-56)

### 2016–2018: Orchestral collaborations and US tour

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: 2016–2018: Orchestral collaborations and US tour")]

From 2016, Singh began incorporating symphony orchestras into his live performances. In February 2016, he performed at the [Dubai World Trade Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_World_Trade_Centre "Dubai World Trade Centre") with an orchestra,[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-57) and later performed at the [Rajasthan Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasthan_Day "Rajasthan Day") celebrations at the [Albert Hall Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Hall_Museum "Albert Hall Museum") in [Jaipur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur "Jaipur").[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-58) That year, he also performed in [Chandigarh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandigarh "Chandigarh") and at [AFAS Live](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFAS_Live "AFAS Live") in [Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam "Amsterdam").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-60)

In 2017, Singh undertook a tour of the United States, performing in cities including [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), [Newark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newark,_New_Jersey "Newark, New Jersey"), and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") The tour featured a symphony orchestra and was attended by large audiences.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-61) He also collaborated with [MTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTV "MTV") and Wizcraft International for the "MTV India Tour" (2017–2018), performing in cities including [Hyderabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyderabad "Hyderabad"), [Ahmedabad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmedabad "Ahmedabad"), and [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-62)

### 2019–2021: North American tours and pandemic period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: 2019–2021: North American tours and pandemic period")]

In 2019, Singh undertook a North American tour, performing in multiple cities including venues such as the [Prudential Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prudential_Center "Prudential Center") in Newark and the [Peacock Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theatre "Peacock Theatre") in Los Angeles.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-63) He also performed at the [Lusail Sports Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lusail_Sports_Arena "Lusail Sports Arena") in Qatar.

During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), he participated in virtual events. In June 2021, he collaborated with Facebook and GiveIndia for a live-streamed relief concert supporting pandemic response efforts in India, which received significant viewership and raised funds.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-64) He resumed live performances in November 2021 at the [Etihad Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etihad_Arena "Etihad Arena") in Abu Dhabi.

### 2022–2026: Arena tours and global performances

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: 2022–2026: Arena tours and global performances")]

In 2022, Singh began a series of international tours across the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), Europe, and Australia.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-65) He also performed a tribute to [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar") on the television special 'Naam Reh Jayegaa' in June 2022.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-66)

## Awards and nominations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Arijit_Singh&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: Awards and nominations")]

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Arijit Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Arijit_Singh "List of awards and nominations received by Arijit Singh")

Singh has received numerous awards and honours in recognition of his work in Indian playback singing. In 2025, he was conferred the [Padma Shri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Shri "Padma Shri"), India's fourth-highest civilian award, by the [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") for his contributions to the arts.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-Padma2025-67)

As of 2026, he has received two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer"), for "Binte Dil" (_[Padmaavat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmaavat "Padmaavat")_) at the [66th National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_National_Film_Awards "66th National Film Awards") in 2019 and "[Kesariya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kesariya_(song) "Kesariya (song)")" (_[Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahm%C4%81stra:\_Part\_One\_%E2%80%93\_Shiva "Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva")_) at the 70th National Film Awards in 2024.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-NationalAwards-68)

Singh has won eight [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Male_Playback_Singer "Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer"), equalling the record set by [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"). His wins include a sequence of five consecutive awards from 2016 to 2020. His eighth award was for "[Sajni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sajni_(song) "Sajni (song)")" (_[Laapataa Ladies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laapataa\_Ladies "Laapataa Ladies")_) at the 70th Filmfare Awards in 2025.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-69) His first Filmfare Award was for "[Tum Hi Ho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tum_Hi_Ho "Tum Hi Ho")" in 2014.

He has also been recognised for his live performances, including receiving the Wizcraft Honour for Best Live Performer and being listed among the top performers at the SSE Arena, Wembley, in the 2016 SSE Live Awards.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-70)

Throughout his career, he has also received multiple [Mirchi Music Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mirchi_Music_Awards "Mirchi Music Awards"), [Global Indian Music Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_Indian_Music_Academy_Awards "Global Indian Music Academy Awards") (GiMA), and [Stardust Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stardust_Awards "Stardust Awards") for his work on films such as _[Ae Dil Hai Mushkil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ae\_Dil\_Hai\_Mushkil\_(film) "Ae Dil Hai Mushkil (film)")_, _[Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy\_(2015\_film) "Roy (2015 film)")_, and _[Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brahm%C4%81stra:\_Part\_One\_%E2%80%93\_Shiva "Brahmāstra: Part One – Shiva")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arijit_Singh#cite_note-GeneralAwards-71)
